# Clinic booking redesign

This project focused on improving the clinic booking experience for patients. The original flow used a color-coded calendar with three separate states. This design created significant confusion for many patients and staff members. We conducted research with the front desk team over two mornings. We discovered that most support calls concerned the calendar interface. This finding guided the direction of the entire redesign process. We decided to simplify the calendar into a single list of times. We also added a clear link for patients who need further help. This change was designed to reduce the number of support calls.

We tested the new flow with eight patients in the waiting room. Six participants completed a booking without any additional assistance. Two participants could not locate the field for insurance numbers. We moved the insurance field to a more visible location. This adjustment addressed the issue identified during the testing sessions. We will continue to monitor the volume of calls in the center. We plan to organize further testing with afternoon patients soon.

This additional testing will help us understand different patient needs. The team remains committed to creating a seamless booking experience. We believe that this approach will deliver meaningful results for patients. This case study demonstrates the value of careful user research. We recommend that future projects begin with similar research activities. This approach will ensure that design decisions remain grounded in evidence. We do not expect the calendar issues to return in the future. We will share additional findings with the wider team next quarter.
